notes: Governing document: the WMU-AAUP agreement 2017-2020 covers all Board-appointed ranked faculty (tenured and tenure-track) as the bargaining unit (1.§1, 2(s)); its Article 27 (Leaves of Absence), 17.§2.4 (tenure clock) and 33.§8 (LTD) set faculty leave. 27.§2 (FMLA) and 27.§8 (paid parental leave) took effect 2018-01-01, before the reference date 2018-02-26; the 2014-2017 FMLA language applied only through 2017-12-31 and is not saved.

2018_00_link (HR Employee Handbook Section 11, Leave Plans) describes leave for non-bargaining employees; its sick-leave rates and annual-leave schedules differ from the agreement's faculty terms, so its provisions are coded with faculty_group naming staff (c18-c23). It cross-references the Policies and Procedures Manual Section 13, not saved.

2018_02_provost_faculty_leave_absence_page is a summary/navigation page: it lists leave types (military, personal, political office, professional, necessity, sick, annual, court, FMLA, funeral) and directs readers to Article 27; no provisions coded from it.

Member's paths. Paid parental leave (27.§8, c1) and the sick-leave path (27.§7.2.7, c2 with the first-two-years 10 days, c3) are alternatives ('may exercise his/her rights under 27.§7.2.7 or 27.§8 but not both'); a member who uses paid parental leave is not eligible for modified duties (27.§7.4, c4/c5), so modified duties are linked in_lieu_of c1. FMLA (c7) runs concurrently with whichever is used (27.§2, 27.§2.6, 27.§7.2.7).

Modified duties (27.§7.4) take two forms: a full workload rearranged with no pay change (c4, other, R16) or a reduced workload with 'some adjustment in compensation and/or in-load teaching or other assignments' (c5, part_time_option, R3). Neither is full-pay relief, so no relief component counts. The semester 'includ[es] the anticipated short-term disability leave'; no separate short-term disability plan is described: pregnancy disability is treated like any other illness (27.§7.3, c17) and paid from the member's sick-leave balance (c9).

Birth-parent chain: paid parental leave 6 weeks (FMLA 12 workweeks concurrent from the start) -> discretionary unpaid leave after FMLA (c8, no stated length). Alternative path: sick-leave use for the birth up to 35 days, own balance (FMLA concurrent) -> up to 10 discretionary paid days for members in their first two years (c3); or modified duties for a semester (c4 or c5), instead of paid parental leave.

Non-birth-parent chain: the same as the birth parent's (paid parental leave and modified duties are for the primary caregiver, role-neutral; sick-leave use for the birth is for either parent): paid parental leave 6 weeks (FMLA concurrent) -> discretionary unpaid leave after FMLA; alternatives as for the birth parent. FMLA also covers care of a spouse with a serious health condition (U5).

Paid parental leave entitlement (c1) is a reading: 27.§8 'shall provide' and 27.§8.1 'shall be granted upon the request' versus 27.§8.2 'may be granted up to six (6) weeks'. Coded guaranteed_on_request with an ambiguous flag; if read as discretionary, the guaranteed figures would lose the 6 paid weeks.

Statutes named: FMLA (c7 for faculty, c20 for staff; 12 workweeks verified against statute text 2026_00_us_fmla_29usc2612). The agreement's FMLA eligibility (one academic year and 1200 hours) differs from the statute's 12 months and 1,250 hours; the agreement's test is recorded. All other named statutes are listed under C4 not_components.

Not components: sabbatical (Art. 26, professional development), professional leave (27.§3.2), court, funeral, military and political-office leaves (cannot be used for a birth), retirement load reduction (35.§4, age 55+ with a retirement date), 27.§2.12 alternative assignment (an employer option to keep a faculty member out of the classroom for the rest of the semester at equivalent pay, not a parental benefit), and the handbook's professional development, university convenience, bereavement and military leaves.
